question: In which Olympic Games did Leander Paes make his debut before winning India's first Olympic tennis medal in the following edition?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Barcelona Olympic Games**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Leander Paes made his debut at the **1992 Barcelona Olympic Games**, representing India in tennis.
 
• He competed in both the singles and doubles events during the 1992 Olympics.
 
• Although he did not win a medal in Barcelona, his debut marked the beginning of a remarkable Olympic journey.
 
• In the subsequent 1996 Atlanta Olympics, Leander Paes won the **bronze medal in men’s singles tennis**, becoming the first Indian to win an Olympic medal in the sport.
 
• His bronze medal in Atlanta was also India’s first individual Olympic medal in 44 years since KD Jadhav’s wrestling bronze in 1952.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atlanta Olympic Games**

 
 
• The 1996 Atlanta Olympics was where Leander Paes won his historic bronze medal in men’s singles tennis.
 
• Paes defeated Brazilian player Fernando Meligeni in the bronze medal match, earning India’s only medal in the Atlanta Olympics.
 
• This achievement marked India’s resurgence in individual sports on the Olympic stage.
 
 
 
• **Sydney Olympic Games**
 
 
• The 2000 Sydney Olympics saw Leander Paes compete in both singles and doubles events.
 
• In the doubles event, he partnered with Mahesh Bhupathi, but the duo did not secure a medal.
 
• The Sydney Olympics was part of Paes’ long-standing Olympic career, spanning seven consecutive appearances from 1992 to 2016.
 
 
 
• **New Delhi Olympic Games**
 
 
• There has never been an Olympic Games held in New Delhi.
 
• India hosted the Asian Games in New Delhi in 1951 and 1982 but has never hosted the Olympics.
 
• This option is incorrect as it does not correspond to any actual Olympic Games.
